transcript.text: How is everybody doing? Welcome back to another Dragon Wilds video. One of the biggest parts of this title, especially
with it having heavy Runescape influence, is your progression through skilling. Now, if you're just starting
out, especially coming into this with a survival crafting mindset, you might be looking at all the skills and wonder
which ones you should actually be focusing on. Now, the first thing I do want to make clear is every skill is
very important in Dragon Wilds. I wouldn't completely ignore any of them, but most of the time these skills are
going to be naturally leveling up just as you're playing the game. So, if you're mining, mining's going to go up.
If you're building, construction goes up. If you're fighting, depending on what combat style you're using, that
combat skill will be going up. There are definitely a few skills that I would pay
more attention to early on because their unlocks can make the rest of the game a lot easier. So, this isn't necessarily
really ranking the best to worst skills overall in the title. This is just the order I would personally prioritize on a
fresh play through, a new world, and a new character. Now, just generally overall, one of the points I would like
to make is you don't necessarily need to grind these skills out very heavily. But, keep an eye on all your skill
tracks and what level you're at with each of these skills. And if you're close to a major unlock, I would heavily
start focusing on that skill specifically to get to that new skill spell, that new ability, that new
passive unlock. It's just going to be very helpful in overall gameplay. So, keep that in mind when we talk about all
these skills. Now, this first one might be pretty interesting to you. This is probably one of the biggest priorities
early on now that it has come to the title, and this would be agility. Agility is useful basically everywhere
because you're constantly moving around Ashen Fall. That's a big heavy part of the title, exploring, gathering
resources, and trying to find hidden locations. Now, you actually are going to be gaining some agility XP simply by
running around on foot, jumping around, and just general mobility. And there are courses throughout Ashen Fall that will
give you a bulk of your XP for this skill, but I would wait to do those courses until you have specific skills
unlocked, which we're about to go over. Now, the reason why why skill is so important is because at level five
you're going to unlock wind step, which gives you much better vertical movement throughout action fall. Then at level 10
you're going to get the double jump. This is one of those unlocks that immediately changes the way you explore
regions. It's going to be so much easier to get to and from areas, up vertical rock faces to the top of point of
interest to find hidden chests and different things like that. Now further on down the skill track you will get an
unlock called the air dash and this is unlocked at level 32. This will give you a horizontal movement while you're
airborne and this thing is super fantastic. Again, once you have these basic skills you can start prioritizing
the agility courses throughout the map to gain XP a lot faster. But overall the biggest reason why this skill is very
important especially early on is passively the skill is going to gradually reduce the stamina you use
while sprinting. So this is not only good while exploring, but it's also going to be good while you're inside of
combat. And then at levels 50 and 75 you're going to get a massive increase to your maximum carry weight. Now those
last two unlocks are especially useful in a survival game where you're constantly bringing resources back to
your base and you're doing resource farms basically. Now agility also opens kibit burrow shortcuts around the map.
It reduces fall damage as you progress and eventually gives you the recall skill. So I wouldn't necessarily sit
there and just grind out agility, but I would absolutely make sure that you're leveling as you're exploring run around
action fall and doing the courses when you find them. Now with this being a survival crafting title and with your
base being the main hub of all your progression I could not pass over the skill of construction. This would
probably be my biggest active priority very early on in the title. You're going to get levels from just building your
base, building crafting stations, but there are some really useful milestones here that I would intentionally work
towards. At level 11 you do unlock the eye of oculus, which makes building larger structures much easier because
you can essentially get a different perspective while you're placing pieces. Now that's not that big of a deal, but
it is very useful. At level 18 you will unlock the oak building tier. And this goes for every single new region. Every
new region in Dragon Wilds has a new building tier for it. You will unlock that building tier once you gather the
necessary resources, but your construction level needs to be high enough to get to that tier. Higher tier
building pieces have higher health, better structural integrity, and just make your bases look way more aesthetic.
But the reason why in my opinion construction is so important and the biggest target for the construction
skill comes at level 40 cuz this unlocks the personal chest spell. Now the personal chest lets you access your own
personal storage remotely at anywhere in the world. And once you combine that with a good supply of law runes and
astral runes, it becomes one of the best quality of life tools in the game in my opinion. It basically gives you a free
inventory that has no weight tied to it. You can dump heavy resources in it, grab something you forgot at your base, or
manage items without physically running all the way home. So if your construction is falling behind because
you've only built a tiny starter house, I would spend some time actually leveling this. Now there are a few ways
you can level this faster, but the game will eventually cap you out. You could sit there and place an inexpensive piece

will eventually cap you and you will be put on basically a timer where you will not gain any XP and it's a game's way of
preventing you from farming this skill because way early in early access, basically what you could do is place
down hundreds of chairs one after the other and level up your construction skill from zero to 99 in in 30 minutes
to an hour. But overall, the personal chest is probably the biggest upgrade for construction and one of the biggest
quality of life upgrades in the title. Now this next skill encompasses virtually every single thing you do in

level 25, runecrafting will allow you to craft fire runes, which are used for certain spells, as well as this is your

50. And this is one of the biggest things I would prioritize very early on for the runecrafting skill. Law runes
are how you travel through lodestones in Dragon Isles, and utility options really

unlocks, like I said, I highly recommend you just farming this as much as possible. It's very easy to do. You can

50 for you to craft. Now, there is an Anima event right next to the church that you can siphon, but you're going to

runes, and it takes a long time to get there because at level 50, it's basically halfway through the skill
track. You want to get there as soon as possible because you are going to be using a ton of law runes in Dragon

runes. Now, keep in mind when you do fast travel, the amount of law runes you use to fast travel to and from

many law runes you're going to be using. Now, this next skill is pretty important
but in my opinion it's at the lower tier of this list. But, this is going to be our artisan. Now, the reason why I say
that is this is probably the skill that you're going to level up passively the fastest because since you're constantly

and using, this skill is going to be leveling up pretty fast. But, one of the milestones that I would pay attention to

You drop all your items that you want to repair on the ground. This can be tools, weapons, armor pieces, jewelry items.
You just dump them on the ground, you cast a spell, all of the items will float in the air, they will repair

get Astral Projection. It allows you to instantly cut down multiple trees at once. And then at level 20, you're going

cut it down, just keep in mind you do have to have Woodcutting level 20 as well as the right tier tool for that
zone that you're in. And Mining does have a similar exploration unlock at level 20 where you can break down

gather the materials that you need and these will climb pretty quickly. Again, if you're close to an unlock, I
recommend you just focusing on it and barreling through it. Now, this next one's going to sound very simple, but
this is your main combat skills. There's three of them in Dragon Wilds. You have your attack skill, which is all melee
combat. You have your range, which is bows. Then you have magic, which is any skill that you're going to be using with
your staff and eventually wands when they do come to the game. And the reason why focusing on these skills are very

Level 23 gives you adaptability, which lets you block or evade without interrupting your melee combo. Range

I said, different enemies and situations favor different approaches and different damage types. But early on I would

You're going to have to use range and magic at some point, especially when it comes to the harder content and bosses.
I highly recommend you to diversify in your combat and and spreading your attention across all three so they are
leveling up together. Now, our last three skills we're going to go over, I'm going to kind of couple them together
because they work in unison. And this is going to be cooking, farming, as well as
fishing. Now, these skills directly feed into one another. Food is a huge part of Dragon Wilds, especially with the

on in the title. Level six, you're going to unlock the grill, which is going to give you another way to prepare your

This is bones to peaches, which gives you another useful source of food while you're out exploring. You basically just

immediately when you set up your first base in Dragon Waltz. Basically, right when you get in Ash and Fall, progress
the main quest a little bit, talk to the old man. Once you place down a small foundation, your bed, whatever it may
be, and you're making a micro base, start farming immediately. The reason for this is farming is not only tied

the ingredients, resources, and plants that you find out in the world, you will have a chance for seeds to drop out of

You're going to need plenty of them, especially when you're progressing into the later regions. So, overall, I would
not ignore farming at all because for a survival crafting title, it does look like something you only do if you enjoy
base building or you want to farm. That's how some other games have implemented this. But a good farm means
a renewable supply of all these ingredients, and those ingredients become food, potions, drinks, and plenty
of different buffs that you're going to be using elsewhere throughout the title. Now, on top of this, fishing is also a
very good skill. Fishing itself is a skill that is probably going to take the longest for you to level. This skill was
probably the hardest to level and took me the longest overall across all the skills in the title. And fishing's very
good because, again, it's going to give you plenty of new ingredients and new recipes when you cook these fish. But
fish-based foods are probably one of the best general healing foods in the game. Fish-based recipes don't necessarily
give you really good buffs, but if you want to have a really good food source that's pretty inexpensive, I recommend
you fishing as soon as possible. You can use rod fishing, but net fishing overall is the best way to not only catch fish
pretty fast, but it's also the best way to level up the skill itself. These are the top skills that I know I'm going to
be prioritizing when 1.0 comes out and I start fresh on a new server, a new character. Now, keep in mind again, you
do not need to sit at your base and grind every skill before continuing the game. You can just naturally progress at
your own pace, whatever it may be. But the better approach is to look through your skill trees, like I said, and find
the next unlock that's actually going to be very useful for whatever you're doing. Then at that point, you can
decide whether it's worth pushing a few extra levels to get there. That's normally how I do my skills. I'm just
naturally doing so many things in the title because, as you know, everything that you do is tied to a skill. But if I

that's going to boost that skill or boost something else that I'm doing out in Dragon Wilds," then I'll just focus
that skill, grind out the XP until I reach that level, and then I'll just continue on or move on to another skill

down in the comments below. I hope this video was at all helpful. This is what I'm going to be prioritizing again when
